summary: Backend-only verification of fire-and-forget transactional emails on POST /api/auth/register (welcome) and POST /api/family/join (joiner + partner-joined). Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_email_triggers.py with 9 tests covering: (a) fresh register returns 200 in <3s, (b) duplicate register → 400, (c) super-admin flag preserved for otilia (login 200 + is_admin=true), (d) 3 back-to-back registers all return 200<3s even while Resend is 429-rate-limiting (confirms fire-and-forget doesn't propagate email errors), (e) family creation + user B join returns 200<3s with 2 members and B.is_me=true, (f) already-in-family → 400, (g) 3rd user joining full family → 400, (h) invalid code (len<4) → 400, (i) non-existent 6-char code → 404. All 9 pass. Full regression: test_password_flows.py (15) + test_forgot_password_rate_limit.py (5) — all 20 pass. Total: 29/29 PASS. Backend logs confirm Resend is currently returning 429 rate_limited, and send_email() correctly swallows the error (logged only) so /register + /family/join responses remain 200 and fast. test@test.com login with test123 verified still working; otilia.ioana96@gmail.com is_admin=true confirmed via login. All TEST_ users (including stale ones from prior iterations) cleaned; no empty families remain.

Actual email delivery will NOT succeed until the Resend rate limit resets or key/domain is provisioned. Not blocking the review request (fire-and-forget semantics verified), but production users are NOT receiving welcome / family-join emails right now.

critical_code_review_comments: Fire-and-forget is implemented correctly: asyncio.create_task(...) is wrapped in try/except in both /register (server.py:497-500) and /family/join (server.py:1276-1285). Even if scheduling fails, response returns immediately.
send_email() (server.py:385-402) catches httpx.HTTPStatusError AND generic Exception — returns None on failure so the awaiting task in create_task never surfaces an exception. Good defensive coding.

_assert_safe_email() runs BEFORE the httpx.post — if a maintainer accidentally injects unsafe HTML/URL it would raise ValueError. Because this runs INSIDE the async task (not the endpoint body), the raise is captured by the caught 'except Exception' in send_email. Good.
Welcome email uses html_escape on user name — no XSS risk.
family/join email dispatch computes partner_name from enriched.members using is_me=False; safe because at this point enriched['members'] always has exactly 2 entries.
server.py is now 1487+ lines — still above the 700-line recommended threshold.
